questions.q: What does 'instance' mean in instance normalization?
options: Each input window is normalized with its own statistics.
The whole data set is normalized once.
Each batch is normalized with the batch mean.

questions.q: Input window [100, 110, 120] (mean 110, population std 8.165). Model output in normalized units is +2.0. What is the forecast?
Which statistics does RevIN use to turn the output back to the original scale?
options: Mean and std of the input window
Mean and std of the training set
Mean and std of the target window
why: The target is unknown at forecast time and using it is leakage.

options: To avoid dividing by zero when a window is flat.

questions.q: A holiday flag (0 or 1) is one of the input channels. What should you do?
options: Do not apply RevIN to it; it is a known calendar feature.
Always apply RevIN to every channel.
why: Correct: normalizing a 0/1 flag per window can make it constant or distorted.
The feature may be very useful.

questions.q: Window [1, 3]: population mean 2, std 1 (ignore eps). gamma = 2, beta = 1. What is the normalized value of 3?
Sales moved from level 100 to level 300. Your model uses global standardization and is now very wrong. What is a good fix to try?
options: Add RevIN or window scaling, and monitor input level drift.
why: Not a fix for level shift.
